criterion_scores.reasoning: I checked the main Stage A/B logic, the write path, and the internal data contract. The skill is thoughtful about PII, HITL, and injection safety, but there are two load-bearing correctness problems: the URL field name drifts between `canonical_url` and `primary_url` (lines 117, 129, 150, 164), and the actual write step does not preserve the earlier URL-first dedup rule, instead instructing title/date/kind backstop dedup (lines 135-139 vs. 164). Because URL identity is central to the artifact's own thesis about avoiding newsletter false merges, these are send-back defects.

I checked whether each stage had all required operational pieces and whether referenced files existed; the supplied reference check says the `.claude/` refs exist. The artifact is very thorough overall, but Stage B relies on `Pipeline/signal-source` in the query without a clear step that ever applies/maintains that label (line 98, contrasted with line 168), and the label-write fallback ledger is only named, not specified enough to execute (line 178). So most required parts are present, but a couple of load-bearing mechanics are incomplete.

I checked the visible house conventions I could verify from the artifact itself: correct project-skill naming/path (no `alex:` prefix), parent-thread-only write discipline for Gmail/Notion/Supabase, subagent used as no-write distiller rather than as a writer, and Supabase positioned as the sanctioned Market-Intelligence store rather than a tombstoned measurement store. I did not find a consequential convention violation in the text supplied.

I looked for over-engineering, resurrected tombstones, duplicated state, and speculative surface. The design is mostly lean and contract-first despite its detail: it keeps writes gated, avoids body-reading the full inbox, and does not introduce banned tools or unnecessary platforming. The one mild risk is state drift from layering allowlist membership with `Pipeline/signal-source` label selection and a possible processed-message ledger, but that reads more like an implementation fragility than a dominant anti-pattern.

I checked whether the artifact is honest about gaps and whether the instructions would be legible to an implementer/debugger. It does many good things here: explicit failure modes, loud-fail guidance for missing `SUPABASE_API_KEY`, and repeated honesty/coverage instructions. But a few phrases are too ambiguous for a safety-sensitive skill: `empty/scaffold` is undefined for stage selection (line 31), `go straight onto the allowlist` muddies the HITL gate (line 49), and the URL naming drift across sections makes debugging the core contract harder than it should be.

defects.quote: Build a Gmail query from its senders/domains + the `Pipeline/signal-source` label
defects.location: ## B1 — Pull bodies from allowlisted senders only
defects.description: Stage B depends on `Pipeline/signal-source` as part of the extraction selector, but the skill never clearly defines when that label gets applied to eligible threads. Later write steps add `Pipeline/processed` and `Pipeline/company-signal` (line 168), and the taxonomy lists `signal-source` (line 215), but no operational step maintains it. That leaves a load-bearing part of the extraction skeleton under-specified and can cause valid allowlisted mail to be skipped.

defects.quote: `primary_url` MUST be the canonical primary source — redirect-resolution is MANDATORY (not optional).
defects.location: ## B2 — Pre-extraction signal filter + structured extraction
defects.description: The artifact's URL contract is internally inconsistent. The schema and dedup/gate text use `canonical_url` (lines 117, 139, 150), but this line switches to `primary_url`, and the write step later uses `url:primary_url` (line 164). Because URL identity is the load-bearing dedup key in this design, the name drift is not cosmetic; it creates real ambiguity about what field downstream logic must populate and compare.

defects.quote: Dedup on (title, event_date::date, kind) as a backstop.
defects.description: This operational write step does not carry forward the prior section's load-bearing URL-first dedup behavior. B3/B3.5 says canonical URL is the primary dedup key and that the run should `GET /event` by URL before writing; here the executable instruction falls back to title/date/kind instead. That reopens the exact false-merge/missed-dedup cases the skill argues against for newsletters and same-day multi-launch events.

defects.quote: fall back to a self-maintained processed-message-id ledger for idempotency
defects.description: A fallback ledger is mentioned for the label-write-blocked case, but the artifact never specifies where that ledger lives, how it is read at run start, or how it is written atomically. As written, the fallback exists as an idea rather than an executable part of the skill.

defects.quote: they go straight onto the allowlist
defects.description: This wording is ambiguous against the stronger HITL invariant elsewhere (lines 21, 61-86) that allowlist changes occur only after Alex approval. The later steps do enforce review, but this sentence makes the safety gate sound automatic in one of the most sensitive parts of the workflow.

defects.quote: Default: if the allowlist is empty/scaffold → `discover`; else `extract`.
defects.description: `scaffold` is not defined, so the default stage-selection rule is not reproducible. Different operators could make different decisions about when the allowlist is still considered scaffold-only.

Reviewed all explicit write paths for parent-thread/MCP constraints, Supabase usage, HITL gates, and PII/logging restrictions.
